reason: Section 10.2 contains separable Committee review topics: meeting and participation rules, grant or partial grant rules, and denial reasons with referral forms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee review meeting and decision process

evidenceText: Within thirty days after the submission of an application for review
Neither the Provincial Archivist nor any representative of the department
may appear before the committee considering an application for review under paragraph 10.1(5)(c)
may inspect the public record in question
A decision of the majority of the members of the Committee

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.2(1) through 10.2(5) govern how the Committee meets, who may participate, inspection during review, and majority finality.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Committee's timing, participation, inspection, and majority-decision rules when it considers an application for review.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee grants and partial inspection of public records

evidenceText: shall grant a request made under paragraph 10.1(5)(a) or (c)
grant the request with respect to a portion of the public record
shall grant a request to inspect a public record made under paragraph 10.1(5)(b)
shall delete the unavailable portion and shall grant the request

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify when the Committee must grant inspection, when it may grant only part of a record, and when severable unavailable portions are deleted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Committee must grant inspection of public records and how it handles partial or severable access.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written denial reasons and referral forms

evidenceText: shall set out in its written decision the reasons for the denial
shall provide the applicant with the forms prescribed by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 10.2(8) separately addresses what the Committee must provide when it denies inspection in whole or in part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Committee's written reasons and referral-form duties when it denies a request to inspect a public record.

reason: Section 10.3 separates the applicant's choice between Court and Ombud routes from the shared in camera inspection power for referred matters.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Referral choice between Court and Ombud

evidenceText: refer the matter to a judge of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick
refer the matter to the Ombud
may not thereafter refer the matter to the Ombud
may not, subject to subsection 10.7(1), refer the matter to a judge

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.3(1) through 10.3(3) define the available referral routes and the consequences of choosing one route.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an applicant may refer a Committee matter to the Court or the Ombud and how one referral route limits the other.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: In camera inspection on referral

evidenceText: may, with respect to any matter referred to them, inspect the public record
such inspection shall be made in camera without the presence of any person

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 10.3(4) is a distinct authority for the Court judge and Ombud to inspect the public record in camera.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the in camera inspection power available to the Court judge and Ombud for referred public-record matters.

reason: Section 10.4 is a cohesive Court review provision covering the hearing, possible orders, copies of the decision, and no appeal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court review hearing, orders, and finality

evidenceText: shall upon the applicant's request hold a hearing
may order the Committee to grant the request in whole or in part
shall order that the Committee
grant the request
deny the request
A copy of the decision
No appeal lies from the decision

proposedGroups.reason: All three subsections address the Court judge's review of a Committee matter and the effect of that decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a Court judge may order on review, who receives the decision, and why the decision is final under section 10.4.

reason: Section 10.5 states one review duty for the Ombud, including the governing authority and 30-day timing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ombud review within 30 days

evidenceText: The Ombud shall in accordance with this Act
review the matter referred to him or her within 30 days

proposedGroups.reason: The section has a single operative rule requiring the Ombud to review a referred matter under the stated authority within 30 days.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Ombud's authority and 30-day deadline for reviewing a referred Archives Act matter.

reason: Section 10.6 is one Ombud recommendation workflow from recommendation to Committee response and notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ombud recommendation and Committee response

evidenceText: advise the Committee of his recommendation
recommend that the Committee grant the request in whole or in part
recommend that the Committee
grant the request in whole or in part
deny the request
shall carry out the recommendations of the Ombud or make such other decision

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections collectively describe how the Ombud recommends an outcome and how the Committee must respond after reviewing that recommendation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Ombud recommends action on a referred request and how the Committee responds and gives written notice.

reason: Section 10.7 is a concise appeal provision tied to dissatisfaction with the Committee's decision after Ombud recommendation review.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeal from Committee decision after Ombud referral

evidenceText: not satisfied with the decision of the Committee under subsection 10.6(3)
may appeal the matter to a judge
Subsection 10.3(4) and section 10.4 apply with the necessary modifications

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the availability and procedural consequences of appealing a Committee decision after the Ombud referral process.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a person may appeal a Committee decision under section 10.7 and which review provisions apply to that appeal.

reason: Section 10.8 contains a single costs rule for matters referred or appealed to a Court judge.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Costs on Court referral or appeal

evidenceText: Where a matter is referred or appealed to a judge
the judge shall award costs in favour of the applicant
where the applicant is successful
if the judge considers it to be in the public interest

proposedGroups.reason: The section identifies when the judge must award costs to the applicant in referred or appealed matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a Court judge must award costs to an applicant in an Archives Act referral or appeal.

reason: Section 10.9 covers several distinct consequences after inspection is granted: access mechanics, language, research undertakings, undertaking breach offences, refusal after breach, and onus in later proceedings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspection, reproduction, fee, and language after access is granted

evidenceText: upon payment of the fee prescribed by regulation
allow the public record or the portion of the public record to be inspected
to be reproduced in whole or in part
shall only be provided in the language or languages in which it is made

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.9(1) and 10.9(2) govern the practical terms for inspection, reproduction, payment, and language once access is granted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the fee, inspection, reproduction, and language rules that apply after a request to inspect a public record is granted.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Research undertaking and Provincial Archivist review

evidenceText: shall not inspect that information until he has completed and returned to the Provincial Archivist an undertaking
shall permit the Provincial Archivist upon the Provincial Archivist's request to review any research notes and drafts

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.9(3) and 10.9(5) impose special undertaking and review obligations when personal information is accessed for research or statistical work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the undertaking and research-note review obligations for access to another person's personal information in a public record.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Breach offence and refusal after undertaking breach

evidenceText: Any person who breaches an undertaking commits an offence
may be refused access to a public record at any time by the Provincial Archivist

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.9(4) and 10.9(6) address the consequences of breaching an undertaking, including an offence and possible refusal of access.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offence and access-refusal consequences that may follow breach of a research undertaking.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Review provisions and onus after refusal of access

evidenceText: apply with the necessary modifications to a refusal of access
the onus shall be on the Provincial Archivist

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.9(7) and 10.9(8) specify the review framework and burden for proceedings after a refusal of access.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which review provisions apply to refusal of access and when the Provincial Archivist bears the onus.

reason: Section 11 contains one evidentiary rule for certified copies of public records signed by the Provincial Archivist.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certified copies of public records as proof

evidenceText: The signature of the Provincial Archivist certifying a copy of a public record to be a true copy
is proof of the fact
shall be deemed to be equivalent to the original record

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the proof and equivalence effect of a certified public-record copy.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the evidentiary effect of the Provincial Archivist's certified copy of a public record.

reason: Section 12 is one offence provision for unlawful damage, destruction, removal, or withholding of public records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Public record damage, removal, or withholding offence

evidenceText: unlawfully damages, mutilates or destroys any public record
removes or withholds from the possession of the Archives or a department any public record
commits an offence punishable under Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act as a category F offence

proposedGroups.reason: The section identifies the prohibited conduct involving public records and the category F offence consequence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the public-record conduct that constitutes an offence and the offence category under section 12.

reason: Section 13 is a single regulation-making authority for Archives Act administration, forms, records, charges, and access exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Archives Act regulation-making authority

evidenceText: The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations
prescribing additional duties of the Provincial Archivist
prescribing a tariff of charges
prescribing the form and manner of applications, referrals and appeals
prescribing exceptions to public records
respecting the transfer of public records to the Archives

proposedGroups.reason: The section lists the subjects on which regulations may be made under the Archives Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main Archives Act subjects for which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations.

reason: Section 14 only repeals the former Archives Act and does not provide a durable study topic from current operative rules.
Section 15 only states commencement by proclamation and the proclaimed date, so it is not a substantive study-map group.

Assessment Act section 1 is a large definitions section, but supplied same-key definition context is truncated before many target definitions, so the full definition grouping should be reviewed by a human.
Section 2 has one current administration rule assigning responsibility to Service New Brunswick; the repealed subsection does not require a separate group.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service New Brunswick administration

evidenceText: Service New Brunswick is responsible for the administration of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 2(1) is the only current operative rule and states who administers the Assessment Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that Service New Brunswick is responsible for administering the Assessment Act.

reason: Section 2.1 contains one delegation authority for the Director to delegate powers or duties to a Service New Brunswick employee.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Director delegation to Service New Brunswick employee

evidenceText: The Director may delegate to an employee of Service New Brunswick
any of the Director's powers or duties under this Act or the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the Director's authority to delegate statutory or regulatory powers and duties to an employee of Service New Brunswick.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall to whom the Director may delegate powers or duties under the Assessment Act or regulations.

reason: Section 3 is a cohesive baseline rule for calculating and levying provincial and local real property taxes on assessments when no other provision applies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Provincial and local taxes on real property assessments

evidenceText: all provincial taxes or rates on real property shall be calculated and levied upon the whole of the assessment
all local government or other local taxes or rates on real property shall be calculated and levied on the whole of the assessment

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections state parallel default rules for provincial and local taxes or rates on real property assessments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default Assessment Act rule for calculating and levying provincial and local real property taxes on assessments.
